clue.text: Sticky period for musicians?

parts.note: read literally, a sticky time like a gooey preserve plus a spell of time; really an informal gathering where players improvise together

explanation.surface: A tricky patch for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: The jam is the improvised playing, not the fruit spread, and the period is the session itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal improvised gathering of players is the familiar term for that kind of rehearsal-free performance.

clue.text: Take off member after first half of July

indicators.note: the member's letters come after the piece from the month
the opening half of the four-letter month name is taken, its first two letters

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a political post early in the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' takes JU from July; 'after' places MP behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off is to leap or spring upward, a synonym.

clue.text: Graduate goes to new York a lot

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate degree
Y is a short form for York, as in the county abbreviation

explanation.surface: A graduate moves to New York and does plenty there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new York' reads as the American city, but new and York each give one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty in number, a synonym.

clue.text: Attractive to look at as it is not hard to see

explanation.surface: Something pretty that is easy to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means good-looking, and read literally it says the eye has no trouble with something visible.

clue.text: Hammer found on the snow?

explanation.surface: A heavy tool lies in the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy hammer is called by this name, and so is a sled used for travel over winter ground.

clue.text: Dish that takes some beating

parts.note: sounds like praise for an unbeatable meal, but the eggs literally have to be whisked

explanation.surface: Praise for a meal that is hard to better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes some beating' is the idiom for excellence; here the eggs are actually beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg dish made by whisking eggs and frying them.

clue.text: Long live the Spanish

parts.note: a toast to the people of Spain, really asking for the Spanish word meaning long live

explanation.surface: A cheer for the people of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Spanish' is not the people but the language: the clue asks for that tongue's cry of long live.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish exclamation of acclaim, literally a wish that someone may live, also used in English.

clue.text: Meant to hold Tom who was involved

indicators.note: the word for meant takes the other piece within it, as if gripping it

parts.note: implied means meant or suggested
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone meant to keep hold of Tom, who was mixed up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name but is a male cat. 'to hold' puts CAT inside IMPLIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mixed up in wrongdoing or shown to have a part in it, a synonym.

clue.text: Surprised sedation's bothering Henry inside

indicators.note: the single letter is placed within the rearranged letters
bothering suggests the word sedation's being disturbed and jumbled up

parts.note: the letters of sedation's, including the S
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone is startled that drugging is upsetting Henry within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothering' rearranges SEDATIONS to ASTONISED, and 'inside' puts H within it. Henry is the electrical unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed or taken aback, a synonym.

clue.text: Performed duties in church perhaps

parts.note: describes carrying out the work of a clergyman, or more generally attending to needs

explanation.surface: Someone carried out their role, possibly at a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to people's needs, especially as a cleric does in a parish.

clue.text: Pat's replacement gaiter

indicators.note: replacement suggests the letters of Pat's are put back in a new order

parts.note: the letters of Pat's, with the S

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for Pat wearing an ankle covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cloth covering for the ankle and upper shoe, a kind of old-fashioned legging.

clue.text: Suitable to become a union member

definitions.text: Suitable to become a union member

parts.words: Suitable to become a union member
parts.note: suggests someone fit to join a trade union, but the union is wedlock

explanation.surface: A worker eligible to sign up to a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The union is not a trade union but a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Old enough or suitable to wed.

clue.text: Churchgoers study going rate amendment

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn

indicators.note: amendment says the words going rate are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Worshippers examine a change in the usual price.
explanation.definitionFit: The assembled worshippers at a service, a collective term.

clue.text: Oust forces in town in east Anglia

indicators.note: the bands of men are placed within the town name

parts.note: DISS is a market town in Norfolk, in East Anglia in England
posses are bands of men summoned to keep order

explanation.surface: Throw out the troops stationed in a town in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the eastern region of England; DISS is a small Norfolk town. 'in' puts POSSES inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone of land or a home, a synonym of drive out.

clue.text: Girl with nothing but party dress these days

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O looks like zero, nothing
a do is an informal word for a party
a mini is a short dress

explanation.surface: A girl wearing only a party dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase dating years of the Christian era, so the present era.

clue.text: Natural to sound well above par on golf-course presumably

indicators.note: says the following description should be heard rather than read

parts.words: well above par on golf-course presumably
parts.note: taking eight strokes on a hole, far over the usual three to five

explanation.surface: Sounds perfectly normal to be well over par on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: Par on a golf hole is three to five strokes, so finishing a hole in eight is well above it; 'in eight' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn and inherent, a synonym.

clue.text: Interplanetary conflict?

parts.note: a fight between celestial bodies, really the famous science-fiction film series

explanation.surface: A battle between worlds.
explanation.walkthrough: Also the nickname of a US missile-defence plan and a famous film saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Battles among heavenly bodies, also the title of a space-opera film franchise.

clue.text: Greek inn the AA rubbished

indicators.note: rubbished suggests the words inn the AA are trashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek dismisses the motoring organisation's hotel guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, known for rating hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Greece's capital, so a Greek.

clue.text: Land quality

explanation.surface: Real estate and its character.
explanation.definitionFit: Land owned is an estate or holding; a quality is an attribute or characteristic.

clue.text: South American footballer's tree

parts.note: SA, abbreviation for South America
Pelé, the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: A Brazilian sportsman's tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of footballer's reads as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African hardwood tree with mahogany-like timber.

clue.text: Fourth-rate lines, rubbish that could bring the house down

definitions.text: that could bring the house down

parts.note: D is the fourth grade after A, B and C
RY, railway, lines of track
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Poor-quality verse and trash that make an audience roar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring the house down' sounds like theatrical applause but here a fungus literally causes a building to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber-destroying fungus that can make a building's structure collapse.

clue.text: Unfeeling — like olive?

explanation.surface: A callous person compared to a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold and pitiless; and literally an olive has a pit in its middle.

clue.text: Second drink transaction

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: A second beer is bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal in which goods change hands for money.

clue.text: Using a key it follows there is an opening

indicators.note: the word it is placed after the first two letters

parts.note: D is a musical key

explanation.surface: With a key there must be a way in.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is musical, D; 'follows' puts IT after AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance passage into a mine.

clue.text: Man with a bit of a problem, ill-disposed

indicators.note: only a small part of the run of words is taken, letters spanning the word break

explanation.surface: A man with a minor difficulty is in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, as in the Swiss author Emil Ludwig.

clue.text: Lie about piece of wood that is material

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about, concerning
a board is a flat piece of timber

explanation.surface: A fib concerning a plank of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A building product made of compressed wood fibres.

clue.text: Young goats, tail first, slip out of control

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for young goats is brought to the front

parts.note: kids are young goats

explanation.surface: Young goats slide around helplessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail first' moves the S of KIDS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To slide uncontrollably, as a car on ice.

clue.text: As the trend developed with everything else

indicators.note: developed suggests the words As the trend are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A fashion grew along with all the others.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands for everything remaining, like et cetera.
